summary_ja: 寒天液に溶き卵と砂糖を加えて型で固めた菓子。人数に合わせて切り分けやすく持ち帰りやすいことから、冠婚葬祭で振る舞う「取り回し」料理として県南地方を中心に親しまれてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: Agar liquid is sweetened and set with beaten egg in a mold — said to be favored, especially in southern Akita, as a 'torimawashi' dish handed round at funerals and celebrations, since it slices easily to serve a crowd and travels well in a box.
source_title: 卵寒天 秋田県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Tofu kasutera — castella sponge made with tofu
summary_ja: 水気を切った豆腐に砂糖や卵を混ぜてカステラ状に焼き上げる菓子。高価だった卵や砂糖の代わりに、ハレの日に食べていた豆腐を使ったのが始まりと伝わる、しっとりした食感が特徴の秋田県南の菓子。
summary_en: Tofu, pressed of its moisture, is mixed with sugar and egg and baked into a castella-style sponge — said to have begun as a way to stretch prized tofu when eggs and sugar were too costly, giving southern Akita a sweet with a moist, tofu-tinged texture.
source_title: 豆腐カステラ 秋田県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Akita asazuke — sweet-and-sour rice dessert with fruit and vegetables
summary_ja: 砕け米をすりつぶして煮た生地を砂糖と酢で味付けし、きゅうりやかぶ、季節の果物を混ぜた甘酸っぱいデザート。一般的な漬物の「浅漬け」とは別物で、田植えを終えた女性たちを癒やす夏の一品と伝わる。
summary_en: Broken rice grains are pureed, simmered, and seasoned sweet-and-sour with sugar and vinegar, then mixed with cucumber, turnip, and seasonal fruit — a summer dessert unrelated to the pickle of the same name, said to refresh women after a day planting rice.
source_title: あさづけ 秋田県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Kamabuku — steamed potato and mochi flour log shaped like fish cake
summary_ja: 茹でてつぶしたじゃがいもに餅粉と砂糖を混ぜ、かまぼこ状に成形して蒸す菓子。魚が手に入りにくい内陸の山間部で、すり身の代わりにじゃがいもを使って考案されたと伝わる、秋田県北の口取り菓子。
summary_en: Boiled, mashed potato is worked with glutinous rice flour and sugar, shaped into a fish-cake-like log, and steamed — said to have been devised in Akita's mountainous interior, where fish was scarce, as a stand-in for fish paste at celebrations.
source_title: かまぶく 秋田県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Akita oyaki — glutinous rice cake filled with sweet red bean
summary_ja: 餅米の生地であんこを包み、こんがりと焼き上げる菓子。野沢菜となすを小麦の皮で包む信州のおやきとは別物で、山の神へのお供えや五城目町の朝市の名物として親しまれてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: Glutinous rice dough wraps sweet red bean paste and is pan-grilled until lightly browned — unrelated to the wheat-and-buckwheat oyaki of Nagano stuffed with nozawana and eggplant, said to be offered to the mountain god and sold as a signature item at Gojome's morning market.
source_title: おやき 秋田県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Sanbai miso — steamed sweet rice-flour and red bean cake
summary_ja: 餅米粉、うるち米粉、小豆あんを茶碗一杯ずつ合わせて練り、蒸し上げる菓子。味噌は使わないが、材料を合わせた見た目が味噌のようだったことが名の由来と伝わる、県南地域の重箱菓子。
summary_en: Glutinous and non-glutinous rice flour and sweet red bean paste, each measured out a bowlful, are kneaded together and steamed — no miso in it, though the name is said to come from how the mixed batter once resembled miso, a tiered-box sweet from southern Akita.
source_title: 三杯みそ 秋田県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

summary_ja: 切った餅を吊るし編みにして水に浸し、冬の寒さで凍らせては乾かす「寒締め」を経て作る保存菓子。さくさくとした歯ごたえが持ち味で、腹持ちがよく、田植えの合間の軽食として食べられてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: Sliced mochi is strung up, soaked in water, then left to freeze and thaw through the winter cold in a process called 'kanjime' — the result crisp and filling, said to have fueled breaks during rice-planting season.
source_title: 干し餅 秋田県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
